text:
The scoreboard said a blowout, but the chances said a coin flip. Seattle beat Calgary 6-1 at Climate Pledge Arena, yet the expected goals finished 2.79 to 2.71, and the simulated replays of every shot split 51 to 49 for the Kraken. Calgary even attempted 83 shots to Seattle's 53. The gap came from finishing and goaltending: Joey Daccord stopped all but one of the 33 shots he faced and saved about 1.7 goals more than expected, while Dustin Wolf allowed six on chances worth 2.79, roughly 3.2 goals worse than expected.

Seattle did its damage early. Berkly Catton scored at 2:22 of the first off a wrist shot that carried only a 13 percent chance, Mackie Samoskevich made it 2-0 with a backhand at 4:40, and Bobby McMann's wrist shot (10 percent) made it 3-0 at 7:40. Shane Wright's backhand, a 9 percent look, stretched it to 4-0 in the second, and Samoskevich added his second late in the period at 19:34. Every one of those goals came at even strength, and none was a high-quality chance, which is how a game that was close in play ended up lopsided.

Calgary did push back, and in the third it generated the better chances, 1.13 expected goals to Seattle's 0.89. Morgan Frost tipped in a power-play goal at 14:25 to break the shutout, but Jordan Eberle answered 39 seconds later with a snap shot to make it 6-1. Samoskevich, with two goals, took first star, ahead of Daccord and Catton, who had a goal and an assist. Brandon Montour logged 23:16 and added two assists.
